card.name: Bihu
card.era: Origins unknown; first recorded 1694; first staged 1962
card.tagline: Joyful Assamese spring courtship dance of the Bihu festival
card.profile: The Bihu dance is an indigenous folk dance of Assam tied to the Bihu festival, especially the spring Rongali/Bohag Bihu in mid-April (Wikipedia). Performed by groups of young men and women, it is characterized by brisk steps, rapid hand movements and rhythmic hip-swaying, traditionally serving as a courtship dance and celebrating fertility and the new agricultural season (Wikipedia). Dancers wear red-themed traditional Assamese attire (mekhela sador for women) and perform to instruments such as the dhol and pepa (hornpipe) (Britannica).
card.insight: The first official record of Bihu dance is said to be Ahom king Rudra Singha inviting dancers to the Rang Ghar fields around 1694; it was first brought to the urban stage in Guwahati in 1962 (Wikipedia).
